title: Chelsea Pride criticises police response to homophobic chanting at Leeds FA Cup tie
content:
LGBTQ+ supporter group Chelsea Pride has criticised the Metropolitan Police’s response to homophobic chanting at Sunday’s FA Cup semi-final against Leeds United.

Chelsea Pride alleged “sustained” homophobic chanting took place in the presence of police across multiple locations at Wembley Stadium but claimed there was no immediate action taken by officers.

Sixteen Leeds fans were reported for consideration of prosecution over homophobic chanting in or around Wembley, the Metropolitan Police said on Sunday, while also saying the match “passed off largely without incident”.

However, Chelsea Pride said: “This position is impossible to reconcile with the lived reality of those present.”

“Sixteen individuals do not represent the scale, volume, or visibility of the abuse witnessed across multiple locations over a sustained period of time,” the group said in a post on X.

The ‘rent boy’ chant, often aimed at Chelsea fans and current and former players, was designated by The Crown Prosecution Service as a homophobic slur in 2022, meaning that those involved could face hate-crime prosecution.

Chelsea Pride described the chanting on Sunday as “widespread and unchecked”, adding that “the gap between what happened and what has been acknowledged is stark”.

“Across key fan areas — including Wembley Park station, Wembley Way and Empire Way, groups of Leeds United supporters repeatedly and openly chanted ‘rent boy’,” the group’s statement read.

“This was not isolated. It was sustained, targeted homophobic abuse, in full public view, before and after the match.

“This behaviour took place in the presence of officers from the Metropolitan Police. They saw it. They heard it. They did not act.

“Even when this was explicitly reported as a homophobic hate crime, there was no intervention.”

The Metropolitan Police has been contacted by The Athletic for comment.

On Sunday, a Metropolitan Police spokesperson said: “Sunday’s FA Cup Semi-Final between Leeds and Chelsea at Wembley passed off largely without incident.

“There were 14 arrests in or around the stadium for offences including GBH (grievous bodily harm), ABH (actual bodily harm), affray, assault on an emergency worker, common assault and tailgating.

“A further 18 people were not arrested but will be reported for consideration of prosecution for other offences. This includes 16 Leeds fans who were seen and heard to be engaged in homophobic chanting.”

Chants referencing the notorious sex offender Jimmy Savile, which have been sung at matches involving Leeds since his death in 2011 despite him having no connection to the football club, could also be heard around Wembley on Sunday.

Leeds have called for Savile chants to be formally recognised as tragedy chants so they can be prosecuted as hate crimes.

A club spokesperson told The Athletic in March: “The club’s supporters are subjected to these sickening taunts at every match by opposition fans, which should not be happening in today’s game and are a disgrace to the victims of Jimmy Savile’s abuse. Equally, the club disapproves of retaliatory chants from our own supporters.”

Chelsea beat Leeds 1-0 courtesy of a first-half Enzo Fernandez goal. They will face Manchester City, who progressed at the expense of Southampton on Saturday, in the final back at Wembley on May 16.
